newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ten Arabs injured in clashes with Israeli forces.
newsitem.headline: Ten Arabs injured in clashes with Israeli forces.

text.p: At least 10 Palestinians were injured on Monday in clashes with Israeli soldiers who beat Arabs trying to stop work on a road for Jewish settlers in the West Bank, witnesses said.

About 100 Palestinians scuffled with some 150 soldiers near Hebron in the most serious outbreak of Israeli-Arab violence since Israel angered the PLO by deciding on Friday to hand over another nine percent of the West Bank.
The PLO, accusing Israel of deceit, wanted at least 30 percent in the first of three pullbacks due to be completed by mid-1998.

Palestinians said the scuffles erupted when an Israeli bulldozer began ploughing through vineyards and almond and olive groves to open a road from the settlement of Kiryat Arba to the Israeli-controlled part of Hebron.
"Palestinians tried to reach the bulldozer to stop it from working and the soldiers tried to beat them back," one witness told Reuters, saying the troops used clubs and rifle butts.
At least five Palestinians were detained, witnesses said. An Israeli army spokeswoman had no immediate information about the incident.

Kawthar Sallam, a reporter for the Palestinian daily al-Hayat al-Jadida, suffered severe bruises when soldiers dragged her by the hair over rough terrain after she tried to cover the scuffles, witnesses said.
She was taken in an Israeli military ambulance to a clinic in Kiryat Arba.
Israel handed most of Hebron to Palestinian authorities in January under a peace deal that left 20 percent of the city under Israeli control.
